3. Mr Mohammad Hossain, the learned Advocate appearing for the accused petitioner, submits that the complaint case filed by the complainant-opposite party under section 138 of the Act is not maintainable in view of the limitation imposed by the proviso of sub-section (1) of section 138 of the Act namely, that if a payee or the holder of a cheque, in due course as the case may be, makes a demand for the payment of the said amount of money by giving a notice in writing, to the drawer of the cheque, within fifteen days of the receipt of the information by him from the bank regarding the return of the cheque as unpaid, ie from the date of first bounce of the cheque, the case must be filed within one month there from and in the instant case, admittedly, the cheque for the first time was presented for payment on 20-8-2001 and when the cheque was dishonoured by the bank of the accused petitioner the complainant opposite party did not serve any legal notice upon the accused petitioner within 15 days from the date of information received by him as to the bouncing of the cheque and admittedly, after the third bounce of the cheque on 8-10-2001 the complainant opposite party served the legal notice on 14-10-2001 after receipt of the information of third dishonour of the cheque and thereafter, filed this case which is contrary to the provisions of aforesaid proviso of sub-section (1) of section 138 of the Act. The learned Advocate for the petitioner further submits that although in the said proviso the words first presentation of the cheque has not been mentioned nevertheless a payee of the cheque if wants to initiate a proceeding under section 138 of the Act he must serve a notice to the drawer within 15 days from the date of receipt of the information from the bank as to the first dishonour of the cheque. The learned Advocate next submits that it is a case wherein the complainant converted the civil liability into a criminal liability under section 138 of the Act and therefore, the provision thereof must be strictly construed and in the instant case since the complainant opposite party is found to have lapsed his right to initiate a proceeding on the first bounce of the cheque there can be no initiation of a criminal proceeding under the provision of section 138 of the Act for subsequent dishonour of the said cheque. The learned Advocate in support of his contention relies on the decision reported in 54 DLR 234 wherein it has been decided by a Division Bench of this court that if a cheque is presented for payment and it is dishonoured it cannot subsequently be re-tendered for payment and if the proceeding is not initiated under the Act within 15 days of the receipt of information of the first bounce the holder or payee of the cheque has no right to initiate any proceeding after presenting the cheque successively. The learned Advocate finally submits that in proviso (b) of sub-section (1) of section 138 of the Act the key word is 'information' and this word 'information' must be read in the light of the expression used in section 154 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (hereinafter called "the Code"). Therefore, the word 'information' which is contemplated in proviso (b) of sub-section (1) of section 138 of the Act must be treated as first information within the meaning of section 154 of the Code. Thus, there cannot be more than one information on the same cheque. That is, in other words, the payee has only one chance or cause of action for initiating a proceeding under the said Act and that is on the first bounce of the cheque. 

 4. Mr Khaled H Chowdhury, the learned Advocate, appearing for the complainant opposite party, on the other hand, firstly submits that the decision relied on by the accused petitioner as reported in 54 DLR 234 is against him and if that decision is considered to be a good decision, he has no case at all because it has been decided by a Division Bench of this court that if the payee or the holder of a cheque in due course, as the case may be, makes a demand for the payment of the said amount of money and it is dishonoured he must give a notice in writing to the drawer of the cheque within fifteen days of the receipt of information by him from the bank regarding the return of the cheque as unpaid and after expiry of the period of 15 days can resort to a criminal proceeding under section 138 of the Act and he cannot initiate a criminal case for subsequent bounce of the cheque. He then submits that this decision is per incuriam, that is, not a binding proceeding inasmuch as before that case the self-same question came up for consideration before another Division Bench of this Court, that is, the case of Habibur Rahman Hawlader vs State and another. In that case the cheque was presented by the payee three times and only after the bouncing of the cheque for the third time the payee served a legal notice upon the drawer and after the failure of the drawer to pay the amount initiated a proceeding under the Act and it was decided by a Division Bench of this court presided over by Mr Md Hamidul Haque J and judgment delivered by Mr Md Monsurul Huq Chowdhury J as his Lordship then was, that the payee can present a cheque for payment as many times as he wants within the period of validity of the cheque as contemplated by proviso (a) of sub-section (1) of section 138 of the Act and if he wants to initiate a proceeding against the drawer of a cheque he can and must do that after serving a notice upon the drawer within fifteen days from the date of receipt of information of bouncing of the cheque and in that case, after the bouncing of the cheque for the third time, the payee served a legal notice upon the drawer and on his failure to make the payment of the amount as demanded he initiated a proceeding and that was found to be a valid proceeding under the Act. But unfortunately, this decision was not reported in any of the legal journals of the country nor this decision was placed by either of the parties before the other bench which decided the case of Abdus Salam vs Md Munshi Rashed Kamal and another (54 DLR 234) though Hawlader's case was decided at an earlier point of time. The learned Advocate then submits that the Howlader's case was taken before the Appellate Division by the accused person and the Appellate Division dismissed the appeal and affirmed the judgment of the High Court Division which has been reported in 53 DLR (AD) 111. Therefore, it has been decided once and for all by the highest Court of the country that a cheque can be presented for encashment as many times as desired by the payee within the period of limitation as contemplated by proviso (b) of sub-section (1) of section 138 of the Act. But unfortunately, this decision was not cited by either of the parties nor was it considered by their Lordships in deciding Abdus Salam's case reported in 54 DLR 234 and therefore, their Lordships arrived at a decision contrary to the decision of the Appellate Division and against the provison of law. Therefore, the learned Advocate submits that the case of Abdus Salam vs Md Munshi Rashed Kamal & another (54 DLR 234) must be considered to be a decision per incuriam. 

 which is equivalent to our section 138 clause (c). Therefore, the Indian Supreme Court emphasised that on each presentation of the cheque and its dishonour a fresh right and not cause of action accrues in his favour. In Howlader's case the Appellate Division approved the judgment of the High Court Division without discussing the law. But on an analysis of the decision the principle of law appears to be that when section 138 has not laid down any limitation on the number of times that a cheque may be presented within the period of six months or any shorter period under clause (a) of the proviso to section 138(1) it will not be desirable to read into the said clause any such restriction as to number of times a cheque may be presented. It is common knowledge that in commercial practice a cheque may be presented any number of times within the period of its validity. The principle of autrefois acquit or autrefois convict will also come into play and the drawer of the cheque cannot be subjected to repeated prosecutions and convictions on the strength of one cheque. So, as there is no restriction with regard to the presentation of the cheque, any number of times within its validity period and it is not open to the court by adding anything more that the cheque cannot be presented for a second time, the theory of double prosecution on the same cheque does not arise. There is no prohibition for presentation of the cheque any number of times within its validity period because the presentation may be in most items at the request of the drawer either in writing or orally but the right to present the cheque within 6 months period is not taken away as that right has already been given to the payee in whose favour the cheque has been given. In this connection it is significant to note that clause (b) of section 141 gives it a restrictive meaning in that it refers to only one fact which will give rise to cause of action and that is the failure to make the payment within 15 days from the date of receipt of the notice. The reason benind giving such a restrictive meaning is not far to seek. Consequent upon failure of the drawer to pay the money within the period of 15 days as envisaged under clause (c) of the proviso to section 138(1), the liability of the drawer for being prosecuted for the offence he has committed arises and the period of one month for filing the complaint under section 141 is to be reckoned accordingly. The combined reading of the above two sections of the Act leaves no room for doubt that cause of action within the meaning of section 141(c) arises and can arise only once. Thus, the settled position of law is that the payee or holder of a cheque in due course can present a cheque as many times as he or she wishes within the period of validity of the cheque and at his or her option can choose on which bouncing of the cheque shall initiate a proceeding under section 138 of the Act. The only limitation is that once on the bouncing of a cheque a notice is served under proviso (b) of section 138(1), the proceeding must be initiated within one month from the date of failure on the part of the drawer to pay the amount within 15 days of the receipt of notice. If after service of notice the drawer fails to pay the amount within 15 days and the payee does not initiate a proceeding within one month therefrom as provided in section 141, the payee forfeits his right to initiate a proceeding under section 138 of the Act. Thus, the decision reported in 54 DLR 234 is per incuriam as it is contrary to the provisions of the Act and Hawlader's case is a good decision.
